chunks.content: # CLO Beginner's Guide: Core Tools - Introduction to CLO Fabrics This document explains the essential procedures and features for working with fabrics in CLO software, covering fabric attributes, material properties, texture application, color management, fabric presets, physical properties, fabric grouping, and saving/loading fabric files. --- ## Overview of Digital Fabric Creation and CLO Fabric Interface This section introduces the process of digitalizing real fabrics, including physical attribute testing and texture scanning, and explains the basic interface for managing fabrics within CLO’s core tools. - Digital fabrics are created by combining physical attribute testing and scanned texture processing. - The CLO fabric tool is accessed via the Library window, specifically under the CLO Training section in Connect. - Pressing **Y** closes the library window. - Fabric properties are managed in the **Attribute Editor** found on the right of the Object window. --- ## Fabric Attributes: Information, Material, and Physical Properties This section details the three main categories of fabric attributes in CLO: information attributes, material attributes, and physical properties, including how to view and edit them. ### Information Attributes - Include fabric name, product code, structure, supplier, and other relevant metadata. - The **Structure** field can be expanded to show fabric ingredients. - Users can edit any field, such as renaming the fabric or updating structure type (e.g., "shrinkage"). ### Material Attributes - Define the visual and tactile appearance of the fabric. - Include texture maps such as **texture** and **hair line**, which are essential stickers for fabric realism. - Color attributes can be customized or selected from libraries. ### Physical Properties - Control fabric behavior under simulation. - Preview effects like hammering under different physical property settings. - These influence the drape, stiffness, and responsiveness of fabric during animation. --- ## Color Management and Application in CLO Fabrics This section explains how to customize and apply colors to fabrics using CLO’s color tools and libraries. - The **Color Tool** consists of: - **User Custom Colors**: Defined by RGB or CMYK values. - **Color Meter**: Samples colors from the screen (exit with ESC). - **Color Libraries**: Includes Pantone, YKK, and ColorRow. - Selected colors are applied directly to the fabric texture. - Two key color adjustment modes: - **Buffer**: Desaturates the base color, converting it to grayscale or black and white to check fabric color accuracy. - Adjustable parameters include **Shadow Intensity** (texture shadow strength) and **Shadow Brightness** (texture brightness). - **Replace**: Quickly swaps base colors while preserving texture detail. - **Color Blocks** can be applied to preview color distribution; cancel to revert. --- ## Texture and Pattern Application and Adjustment This section covers how to add, adjust, and manipulate fabric textures and patterns. - Fabric textures are image files containing texture and color information. - Textures can be added by dragging files from the library or local folders into the material window.

chunks.content: - Adjustable parameters include **Shadow Intensity** (texture shadow strength) and **Shadow Brightness** (texture brightness). - **Replace**: Quickly swaps base colors while preserving texture detail. - **Color Blocks** can be applied to preview color distribution; cancel to revert. --- ## Texture and Pattern Application and Adjustment This section covers how to add, adjust, and manipulate fabric textures and patterns. - Fabric textures are image files containing texture and color information. - Textures can be added by dragging files from the library or local folders into the material window. - Texture editing tools allow: - Scaling (enlarge/shrink) - Rotation - Position adjustment in both 2D and 3D views - Precise size adjustments can be made by right-clicking textures and entering numeric values. - Users can create new libraries and folders to organize materials. --- ## Line Art and Additional Fabric Effects This section explains adding line art to enhance fabric realism and how to manage front/back fabric materials. - Line art adds details such as wrinkles or creases to simulate fabric girling effects. - Line art can be added from the drawing library, selecting color and line style. - Users can adjust the line art strength and see real-time effects in the 3D window. - Line art can be deleted via the trash can icon. - Fabrics can have different materials assigned to front and back sides: - Disable "use same material on front" to assign separate back materials. - Adjust back material properties independently. --- ## Fabric Presets and Material Types This section provides an overview of fabric presets and common material types used in CLO. - Fabric presets include a wide variety of materials categorized by type. - Material types often applied to fabrics include: - Gloss fabrics - Silk - Leather - Tanning cloth - Fur - Wool - Other material types used for accessories and props include: - Glass - Necklaces - Lights - Gems - Metals - Material effects should be checked in the rendering window to verify appearance. --- ## Adding, Managing, and Applying Fabrics This section details how to add new fabrics, duplicate and edit existing fabrics, and apply fabrics to clothing panels. - Add fabrics using the **plus sign** in the material window or drag from the sketchbook or local folders. - The sketchbook contains common fabrics for quick use. - Fabrics can be copied and modified (e.g., change color) to create variations. - To apply fabrics: - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** to select clothing pieces (e.g., belt panel). - Drag desired fabric from the material window onto the selected piece. - Fabrics can be reordered by dragging in the material window. - Rename fabrics by double-clicking their names. --- ## Fabric Grouping and Organization This section explains fabric grouping for complex garments and fabric cleanup tools. - Create fabric groups in the material window to organize multiple layers or garment pieces. - Drag fabrics between groups for better management.

chunks.content: - To apply fabrics: - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** to select clothing pieces (e.g., belt panel). - Drag desired fabric from the material window onto the selected piece. - Fabrics can be reordered by dragging in the material window. - Rename fabrics by double-clicking their names. --- ## Fabric Grouping and Organization This section explains fabric grouping for complex garments and fabric cleanup tools. - Create fabric groups in the material window to organize multiple layers or garment pieces. - Drag fabrics between groups for better management. - Delete fabrics using the trash can icon or right-click menu, which offers options to delete unused or specific fabrics. - Reset fabric restores it to the default state. - Groups can also be deleted individually. --- ## Fabric-Fabric and Fabric-Object Relationships This section clarifies how fabric assignments correspond to clothing objects and how to identify applied fabrics. - Clicking a fabric in the material window highlights the clothing pieces it is applied to. - Fabrics applied to specific garment parts are highlighted in yellow. - Selecting garment parts highlights the corresponding fabric in blue. - This visual correlation aids in fabric management and editing. --- ## Saving and Opening Fabric Files This section covers saving fabric setups for reuse and loading existing fabric files. - Fabrics can be saved in **ZFAB** format via the Save option. - Users can rename the fabric during saving. - Saved fabrics can be reopened by selecting the file through the Open command. - This allows transferring fabric properties between projects or sharing fabric assets. --- # Summary This guide thoroughly covers fabric creation and management in CLO, including physical and material attributes, color and texture application, fabric presets, physical simulation properties, grouping, and file management. Understanding these tools provides users with the ability to create realistic, customizable digital fabrics for 3D garment design and simulation.
